clue.text: Hit Philip with eastern weapon

parts.note: a blow is a hit
Pip is a short form of Philip, as in Great Expectations
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a man called Philip with a weapon from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern weapon' reads as one phrase, but 'eastern' belongs to the wordplay and only 'weapon' defines. Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, Philip Pirrip.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts are propelled by breath, a hunting weapon associated with Asian and South American peoples.

clue.text: Post openings of love letters penned by committee

indicators.note: whatever is penned is shut inside an enclosure, so one piece ends up held within another

parts.note: a board is a governing committee

indicators.note: an opening is where something starts, so only the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A committee drafts love letters to be sent in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, which suits the love letters, but it is a noun meaning a short pillar, and the committee is the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short sturdy pillar, such as one blocking vehicles or for mooring ships, so it is a kind of upright stake.

clue.text: One admitting wife in Nevadan city is upset

definitions.note: to own up is to admit, so an owner is taken as one who owns, i.e. admits

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something turns it upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
one piece placed inside another is literally in it

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone lets his wife into a Nevada city, which is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno is famous for quick divorces, which makes the wife sound like the story. RENO turned over is ONER, and W slips in after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, in the older sense of owning up, means to confess or acknowledge, so an owner is playfully someone who confesses.

clue.text: New paper established — it's agreed beforehand

indicators.note: something made new has been remade, so its letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a fact established is a fact proved

explanation.surface: A newspaper has been founded with everything signed off in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New paper' reads as a fresh newspaper, but New is only the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Preapproved describes something given approval before it is formally requested or needed, so it was consented to in advance.

clue.text: Walk in the park, and what comes next?

parts.note: surface reading: a stroll through a park; setter's reading: an idiom for a very easy task
setter's reading: after a stroll in the park you might well sit down to eat outdoors on a rug

explanation.walkthrough: Both the easy-task idiom and the outdoor meal fit one word: the idiom 'no picnic' means hard work, and a meal on the grass naturally follows a park stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Picnic is informal for an easy task, matching the idiom for something effortless, as well as an outdoor meal.

clue.text: Inferior blessing not entirely needed

indicators.note: if a word is not entirely needed, only a stretch from inside it is used and the rest is thrown away

parts.note: the middle stretch of this word, dropping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A second-rate blessing that nobody really needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside b-LESS-ing once the opening B and closing ING are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Less can mean lower in rank or importance, as in 'no less a person than', so it serves as a synonym for lower-grade.

clue.text: More than enough to support former partner, for instance

definitions.note: a phrase meaning 'as an illustration', standing for the noun

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands underneath, so it is written after the other

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: Paying generous maintenance to an ex, to give one case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' suggests alimony, which goes with the former partner; in a down answer it just places AMPLE below EX.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For instance' introduces an illustrative case, and an example is exactly such an illustrative case.

clue.text: Small ice cream cake

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a cone is an ice cream served in a wafer

explanation.surface: A little ice cream cake on a dessert menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one dessert, but 'ice cream cake' splits: S + CONE, then the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small plain baked item, often eaten with jam and cream, a kind of light teatime bun.

clue.text: Fine material wrapping new blade

indicators.note: a wrapping goes all round its contents, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A delicate fabric wrapped round a new knife for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' sounds like praise of the material, but 'Fine material' together is the delicate fabric that goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long pointed weapon, and also a surgeon's cutting tool, so it stands loosely for an edged instrument.

clue.text: Elegant silver over in US city

parts.note: chic means stylish
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Smart silverware turned over in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like an instruction to turn something round, but it simply supplies O; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major city in Illinois on Lake Michigan, one of the largest urban areas in America.

clue.text: Spell in prison headquarters initially overlooked

indicators.note: what is overlooked at the start is missed out, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the can is slang for prison
a station, as in police station, is a base of operations

explanation.surface: A stretch inside, with the prison headquarters turning a blind eye at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell in prison' reads as a jail term, but Spell is the definition. The can is slang for prison, and headquarters is a station, as in police station.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation is a set of words chanted to work magic, which is what a magic spell is.

clue.text: American/Irish song

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A ballad from the Irish-American tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash makes it look like a hyphenated heritage, but the two words just give two abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, especially a simple traditional one, as in 'Londonderry Air'.

clue.text: Indian Premier League welcomed by member of royal family, 23

definitions.note: a cross-reference: the answer to 23-across, STANDARD

indicators.note: someone welcomed by a host is taken in, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a prince is a male royal
IPL is the standard abbreviation for the cricket league

explanation.surface: A royal hosts the Indian cricket league.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian Premier League is a major professional cricket competition, known everywhere by its initials; 23 points to the answer at 23-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a rule of conduct or moral benchmark, so it is a standard in the sense of a norm one lives by.

clue.text: Leave Antarctica?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a very dry region, which the frozen continent technically is

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the surprise: Antarctica gets so little precipitation that it counts as the largest desert on Earth, despite all the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon, and a desert is any region with very low rainfall, a classification Antarctica meets.

clue.text: Coe isn't running district

indicators.note: while running, the parts are in motion and get jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe is not competing in the local area.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a famous British Olympic middle-distance runner, which makes 'running' look literal; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a distinct part of a town or region, much as a district is one administrative part of an area.

clue.text: Upset, wearing green

parts.note: dressed in something is wearing it
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone upset, dressed in green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as an emotion, but it is the verb: to knock over. Vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert is to turn something upside down, which is what upsetting a vase or boat does.

clue.text: Double act slow to riff, so fall behind ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the end letter of each word is kept

parts.words: act slow to riff, so fall behind
parts.note: the final letter of each of the eight words

explanation.surface: A comedy duo takes its time with a riff and so falls behind in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double act' looks like the definition, but only 'Double' is; 'act' starts the run of final letters, which spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold means having two parts or being twice as great, which is exactly what double means.

clue.text: Alarm following fit

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
fit and right both mean suitable or proper

explanation.surface: Panic after a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' suggests a seizure, which goes with alarm, but here it means proper, as in 'fit and proper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of fear, and alarm is that same sudden fearful feeling.

clue.text: Failing like gun turned the other way around

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: something turned faces the opposite direction, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: as and like both mean 'in the manner of'
to gun an engine is to rev it

explanation.surface: A failing, like a gun pointed back at its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a weapon, but it is the verb, as in gunning an engine. AS + REV, run backwards, is VERSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is a Latin phrase meaning with the order reversed, used when the converse also holds.

clue.text: Shade of some Levi's originally

indicators.note: taking only some of the words means a run of letters across them is used

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A colour that some Levi's jeans first came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' and 'originally' suggest a denim colour, but the answer runs across le-VI'S OR-iginally.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the projecting brim of a cap that keeps sun out of the eyes, a kind of eyeshade.

clue.text: I hate this short novel?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an exclamation of disapproval

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A reader complains about a novella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short novel' looks like a novella, but it means a book cut short: BOOK loses its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is the exclamation an audience shouts to show contempt, the spoken equivalent of declaring dislike.

clue.text: Like dog to upend wood

indicators.note: upending turns something on its head, which in a down clue makes the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: as and like both mean 'in the manner of'
a lab is a Labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A dog digging up a pile of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab is short for Labrador, a dog breed. AS + LAB, turned over, gives BALSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models and rafts.

clue.text: At first, some heard, I nearly dominated in Green Party

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.words: some heard, I nearly dominated in Green
parts.note: the first letter of each of the seven words

explanation.surface: An early boast from a candidate who almost swept the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Party' reads as the political party, but Green is the last word of the initials and Party alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively social gathering or celebration, such as a dance.

clue.text: Pigs' blood putting off outsiders in White House

indicators.note: putting off those on the outside sends away the end letters, keeping the inner part

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A crude insult about Washington, calling the police 'pigs' and shedding blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' points to Washington, but taken literally it is a house made of snow. Both words lose their outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome shelter built from blocks of snow, so it is literally a house that is white.

clue.text: Disgusting position

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a place in a hierarchy

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like a revolting stance; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul or offensive as an adjective, and a level or grade in a hierarchy as a noun.

clue.text: Model bear next to A road

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, tolerate it
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A model posing beside a bear on a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning tolerate. 'A road' also echoes the British A-road, a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A model as an ideal to copy is a benchmark or exemplar, which is what a standard is.
